title: Raiders Ride Running Game, Defeat Texans In 2nd Preseason Contest
description: Aidan O’Connell sparked a gritty second-half comeback in Houston, overcoming a shaky start from top pick Fernando Mendoza to secure a narrow victory behind a dominant rushing attack.
fullText:
The preseason games don't matter much at all when it comes to wins and losses, but it does matter for teams to see what their players can do.

The Las Vegas Raiders defeated the Houston Texans on Thursday, 22-20, on the road. It also marked the first start of Fernando Mendoza's career, although it could've been better for the No. 1 overall draft pick.

The Texans began the scoring with Woody Marks punching in a 20-yard rushing touchdown just five minutes into the game.

Then, not even two minutes later, Mendoza threw a pick-six as Wade Woodaz intercepted the pass and returned it 80 yards for a score.

Mendoza backed up and threw the ball into a tight space with the defender right there, and Woodaz had no problems scoring.

FERNANDO MENDOZA THROWS A PICK SIX 😳

Welcome to the NFL.

(via @NFL)pic.twitter.com/3kHqZrcGhk

Aidan O'Connell, the Raiders' third-string QB, played the rest of the way and went 15-of-24 for 166 yards.

As a matter of fact, the only touchdowns for the Raiders both came from the running game. Dylan Laube, a sixth-round pick in 2024 from New Hampshire, scored towards the end of the third quarter, and he finished the game with 37 yards on six carries.

Dylan Laube takes it in for the TD and does his dance 🕺

LVvsHOU on ESPN
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ASCka61RNq

Veteran RB Dare Ogunbowale, who played the past few seasons with the Texans, scored with just over seven minutes to go.

He finished the day with 35 yards on four carries, and rookie Mike Washington Jr. had 56 yards on nine carries with former Indiana RB Roman Hemby registering 27 yards on six carries.

In total, the Raiders had 159 yards rushing and 400 yards of total offense.

Dare Ogunbowale turns on the jets for the TD 💨

LVvsHOU on ESPN
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FyXEH62TVn

While it doesn't matter too much, the Texans were up 20-3 going into halftime, and the Raiders snuck out the hard-fought win.

O'Connell had the game-winner, as the Raiders QB ran for a one-yard touchdown in the closing seconds, although the extra point was missed.

RAIDERS TAKE THE LEAD LATE!!

LVvsHOU on ESPN
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/WQKAH0lJTH

The Texans actually had a chance to get into field goal range, but Devin Lafayette had the game-sealing interception as veteran Brett Rypien threw the final pass of the game for the Texans.

Devin Lafayette calls GAME with the INT 🔥 pic.twitter.com/YxQVZXPxva

The Raiders have one preseason game remaining, which comes on Thursday, August 27, against the San Francisco 49ers in Las Vegas, and it will be worth watching to see how many notable players see any meaningful minutes.

title: Chargers throttled by 49ers in preseason game: Recap of LA's loss
description: A brutal 41-17 blowout exposed depth issues for the Los Angeles Chargers. Read our full breakdown to see how the game played out.
fullText:
The Chargers suffered a tough reality check at SoFi Stadium, falling 41-17 to the 49ers in their second preseason matchup.

Here is our recap of Thursday's game:

The Chargers' coverage unit gave up an 83-yard punt return touchdown to 49ers wide receiver Jacob Cowing, followed closely by a seven-yard rushing score from running back Sincere McCormick. The quick sequence of breakdowns put the Bolts in a huge hole.

CB Rodney Shelley: 2 passes defended

Head coach Jim Harbaugh stood firm by his pregame promise: the starters were scheduled for exactly one series, and one series only. Ultimately, quarterback Justin Herbert's first live-game exposure lasted a mere three snaps before the unit went three-and-out and trotted back to the sideline. Herbert completed a single nine-yard pass but missed wide receiver Ladd McConkey on third down

Quarterback Trey Lance relieved Herbert against his former team and showed off his athleticism, turning a collapsing pocket into a 37-yard run to set up a field goal. As a passer, Lance finished 10-of-16 for 76 yards.

Quarterback DJ Uiagalelei found the going much tougher this week after his solid opener last week. Despite a garbage-time passing touchdown, Uiagalelei completed only seven passes on 15 attempts for 80 yards.

Largely due to the inability to generate any push or create holes up front, Chargers running backs combined for 24 yards on 16 carries.

The offense was plagued by multiple procedural penalties that wiped away some of the best gains of the first half. These mental lapses consistently put the offense in unfavorable behind-the-chains situations, contributing heavily to a 2-for-14 third-down conversion rate.

Defensively, linebacker Junior Colson's pick-six was a bright spot, as he picked up where he left off after a solid performance last week. Colson is vying for a roster spot alongside Del'Shawn Phillips, and one more dominant outing could land him on the final 53.

The Bolts' run defense and tackling was undisciplined all night, ultimately surrendering 146 rushing yards (4.1 yards per carry) and three touchdowns.

Cornerback Rodney Shelley was targeted quite a bit in this game, but managed to break up two passes. Shelley has raised eyebrows this summer and is currently pushing for one of the final spots.

There wasn't an edge rusher who pulled ahead for the fifth spot, but I was intrigued by what I saw from Andre Carter II, who the Chargers signed before the preseason. Carter flashed as a pass rusher.

Special teams coordinator Ryan Ficken will have plenty of film to correct this week after the coverage unit allowed the explosive 83-yard touchdown return to Cowing. Returner Devonte Ross also fumbled an ensuing kickoff, setting up an easy 49ers score.

The Chargers will head back to the drawing board and the practice field to clean up these execution errors before wrapping up the exhibition season and finalizing their 53-man roster next Thursday, August 27, against the Rams at 7:00 pm PT.

This article originally appeared on Chargers Wire: Chargers throttled by 49ers in preseason game: Recap of LA's loss

title: Paige Bueckers Tells Caitlin Clark To “Calm Down” After Tense Play
description: Popular WNBA stars Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers are arguably the two most popular players in the league, but that doesn’t mean they always get along. The Dallas Wings scored a major home victory over the Indiana Fever on Thursday night. However, the most memorable moment of the game featured tension between the two stars. […] The post Paige Bueckers Tells Caitlin Clark To “Calm Down” After Tense Play appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Popular WNBA stars Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers are arguably the two most popular players in the league, but that doesn't mean they always get along. The Dallas Wings scored a major home victory over the Indiana Fever on Thursday night. However, the most memorable moment of the game featured tension between the two stars. Clark was visibly upset about getting played with hard defense and gave Bueckers a slight shove at the end of the tense exchange.

Bueckers had a funny viral moment telling Clark to "calm down" after the situation escalated and the two had some space between them:

Clark has had some issues with other players in the league due to getting met with hard defense as the lead guard and engine of the offense. The past incident with Alyssa Thomas led to political news television stations getting involved in the drama.

Bueckers and Clark got tangled up here until the latter shoved the former away while arguing with the officials. Clark clearly looked more upset since she has talked about not feeling like she gets fair foul calls from the referees. The funny reaction of Bueckers saying to calm down showed how chill she was in the tense moment.

Bueckers entering the WNBA just one year after Clark sees them on almost the same exact timeline. Just one season separates their experience level as both hope to become MVP candidates and WNBA Champions over the next few seasons entering their prime years.

Both seem to have opposite fan bases, and that can play a role in a rivalry taking off. Bueckers has won over the diehard WNBA fan to follow before the new core of stars entered the league. Clark has a lot of casual fans who clash with the WNBA fan base and what the league has done before her.

One could argue that Clark has a rivalry with Angel Reese already, but both play different positions. Bueckers is a guard and has an equally high ceiling to Clark to become the best female player in the world. Both ladies are destined to have some playoff matchups, but the tension here shows a feud could easily happen.

A lot of the WNBA coverage this season has focused on outside things, like politicians backing up Sophie Cunningham's comments on trans athletes. Indiana has dealt with a lot of this due to right wing figures trying to take ownership of their fan movement.

However, the actual basketball on the court is likely the bigger reason for tense interactions and technical fouls this season. All eight WNBA playoff teams are having strong seasons, with most believing they have a real shot at the WNBA Championship.

Three weeks off for the FIBA Basketball tournament will see seeding mostly decided over the next week. All these games are important for postseason standings, so it makes sense that players like Clark and Bueckers are on edge. Luckily for Dallas fans, Paige seems ready for the moment since she came off more poised here.

Like HEAVY's content? Be sure to follow us.

title: Jaguars Set to Take on Panthers in Second Preseason Game
description: Roster spots hang in the balance as Jacksonville returns home for its second preseason game. Roster spots are on the line, and all eyes will be focused on whether backup QB Nick Mullens can rebound after last week's poor outing.
fullText:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to square off against the Carolina Panthers in the team's second preseason game, first at home, Friday at 7:30 PM.

There will only be one preseason game left after this one, so players fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster are running out of time to separate themselves and prove they deserve to make the team. Friday night will be a pivotal opportunity for all who don't already have their jobs locked up for the upcoming season.

What are some of the main storylines to follow during Friday's game?

After not playing his starters in last Saturday's opener against the New Orleans Saints, head coach Liam Coen has not given a definitive answer as to whether they will see any action in this game.

It looked like Coen was leaning towards playing the starters this week after they didn't have a great showing during their joint practice with the Saints. However, after Wednesday's dominant showing by the starters in a joint practice with Carolina, especially the run game, it looks like Coen has changed his tune and is now leaning in the other direction.

With starters across the NFL rarely playing in their team's final preseason game, it appears that Jacksonville's starters will enter the regular season without seeing any preseason action at all. Hopefully, the joint practices and remaining team practices will have the starters ready to go for opening day.

Backup quarterback Nick Mullens had a dreadful showing last week against the Saints. He has not looked very good throughout the offseason, leading to concerns about whether the Jaguars should look to upgrade their QB2 spot. With options like Anthony Richardson and Mason Rudolph likely available in potential trades, Mullens needs a strong showing to quiet the growing whispers that the Jaguars may be better off finding a new backup for Trevor Lawrence.

The Jaguars have seen their offensive line decimated by injuries. Cole Van Lanen, who was expected to be the starting left tackle this season, was activated from the PUP list on Thursday after a late-season injury sidelined him all offseason. His immediate replacement, Walker Little, struggled to fill in for Van Lanen at LT and was replaced by Anton Harrison, who has been the team's starting right tackle the last three years.

It looks like Harrison's switch to LT is permanent, as he was listed as the starter there on Jacksonville's first depth chart. When CVL is ready, he will likely take over at RT.

Now, Little is also injured. As is guard Wyatt Milum, who was in the running to take over for starting right guard Patrick Mekari, who recently underwent back surgery and is expected to be out for a significant period.

Milum is expected back next week, so at least that is a positive. Reserve Chuma Edoga also suffered an injury in the Jaguars' preseason opener and is still working his way back.

The beneficiary of all these injuries has undoubtedly been rookie Emmanuel Pregnon. Jacksonville's third-round pick was one of the few Jaguars' draft picks to receive high grades and had a very encouraging debut against the Saints. Pregnon may wind up as a Week 1 starter as a result of all these injuries. If he earns a starting job to open the season, it may be very difficult for anyone to wrestle it away from him.

The battle between Ventrell Miller and Branson Combs to win Devin Lloyd's starting linebacker job has not yet been settled. While the Jaguars' starters were rested last week, both Miller and Combs saw playing time as each continued his push to win the job.

Both will presumably be on the field against the Panthers. Will either be able to separate himself from the other?

With the regular season right around the corner, Friday night's game gives many players a key opportunity to prove their worth.

There are still several roster spots, and at least one starting job, up for grabs with only about three weeks to go before the real games begin. Many players will be looking to make a statement Friday night.

Hopefully, the players can all have a good showing, and the team can come out of Friday's game without suffering more injuries.

title: Dream star Angel Reese perfect, gets historic double-double vs. Sparks
description: Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese didn't miss a shot, joining an exclusive club with her double-double against the Los Angeles Sparks
fullText:
Angel Reese, not far removed from missing two close-range buckets in a loss she said kept her up at night, recorded a historically flawless performance in the Atlanta Dream's 124-88 win over the Los Angels Sparks on Thursday.

Reese went 9-for-9 from the field with two 3-pointers in the victory, finishing with 20 points, 10 rebounds, eight assists and three steals. She's just the third player in WNBA history with a 20-point double-double on 100% shooting.

She also had three offensive rebounds in the first half to break her own WNBA season record of 172 from 2024.

It was Reese's WNBA-leading 25th double-double of the season. With eight games left in Atlanta's regular-season schedule, she needs four more such performances to beat Alyssa Thomas' single-season record of 28 double-doubles, set in 2023.

There's more to add to the résumé for Reese, who also set a Dream franchise-high mark on Thursday for field goals without a miss.

"I was just in the mode. When you see the ball go through the net, you just continue to shoot it. I think the defense really led to the offense, and we got a lot of deflections," Reese told reporters. "So, I kind of knew what kind of game it was going to be from the first steal I got, and just continuing to fight through."

The perfect night comes after the disappointment of losing Sunday's overtime matchup against the Indiana Fever, which saw Reese miss two late layups that could have won the game in regulation.

"I didn't sleep. The competitor in me wanted to win that game so bad," Reese said Tuesday night. "I replayed that play so many times."

Atlanta has responded with back-to-back wins, including Tuesday's victory over the reigning WNBA champion Las Vegas Aces.

Reese has combined for 41 points, 20 rebounds and 12 assists over those two games.

"She's had two excellent games since then," Dream coach Karl Smesko said of Reese's play since Sunday. "Today was just outstanding, and hopefully it's just something to build on from here."

The last player to record a 20-point double-double without missing a single shot was Los Angeles Sparks center Nneka Ogwumike, 10 years ago. Ogwumike had 32 points and 10 rebounds when she did it, in a win over the Dallas Wings on June 11, 2016.

A WNBA champion, league MVP, All-Star and president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association, Ogwumike announced on Wednesday that she'll be retiring at the end of the season.

It gave the performance extra meaning for Reese, who joined Sports on Prime's broadcast after Thursday's win and spoke about her admiration for Ogwumike.

"It means a lot, I mean Nneka has poured into me since I've been in the league. She's done so much for us, being able to be the president and being able to pour into the next generation," Reese said. "A lot of things that we have right now is because of her. She was one of the people that built this house here in LA and being able to see her legacy continue 15 years — a very long time. To see how flawless she continues to be day in and day out, I'm really proud."

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY Sports: Dream star Angel Reese perfect, gets historic double-double vs. Sparks

title: Springboks v All Blacks: The players that could define first Test
description: South Africa and New Zealand collide in the first of four Tests in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series
fullText:
After a week of jawing over the complexities of rugby's lawbook and the speed of the game, South Africa and New Zealand will – mercifully – at last clash in the opening encounter of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series in Johannesburg.

Both Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie, the sides' respective head coaches, have been pointed in their press engagements ahead of the first Test as they perhaps seek to put a bit of pressure on the officials ahead of four back-to-back Tests between the two heavyweight nations.

There was plenty to consider in the selections made by the Springboks and All Blacks, not least the world champions omitting captain Siya Kolisi – though working his way back from injury, the flanker trained this week and could have been picked had Erasmus so chosen.

The installation of Paul de Villiers nonetheless comes with the breakdown likely to be a key battleground, and the tourists can welcome Ardie Savea back into the fold to bolster their back row.

A fascinating clash of tactics could well be in store at Ellis Park – here are five individuals who could be decisive:

Let us begin with the Springboks' openside, who has been rewarded for his strong Nations Championship form with selection ahead of Siya Kolisi. De Villiers has a classical scavenger's build, and will surely be tasked with disrupting the All Blacks' ball, with New Zealand making no secret of their desire to play with pace.

There is plenty of jackal threat within this South Africa pack, which has not always been the case. Malcolm Marx and Jasper Wiese are both proficient over the ball, and how referee Matthew Carley handles their attempts to stymie and stall New Zealand possession could be pivotal – particularly with the All Blacks having shown such willingness to play multiphase, even in their own half.

Equally instructive is the make-up of New Zealand's back row. Ardie Savea's return at No 8 is no surprise after the captain was cotton-wooled for the tour matches, and Vaa'i's selection on the blindside had similarly appeared likely after his successful deployment there against Ireland in July. Vaa'is is a strong carrier but crucially provides an extra long-limbed lineout jumper to match South Africa's Pieter-Steph du Toit. The All Blacks' attack has shown some nice attacking variety in their lineout launch plays since attack coach Mike Blair, the former Scotland scrum half, arrived alongside Rennie, and Vaa'i may help free up Savea.

There is a risk, though, to the selection. With Vaa'i in the starting side to cover, New Zealand have eschewed a lock on the bench and perhaps look a little lightweight with Anton Segner and Peter Lakai two of their five forward replacements. Could the heft and experience of Patrick Tuipulotu have been preferred? Segner and Lakai will be tasked with upping the intensity in the final quarter but matching the Springboks physically will be key.

It says a lot about the manner in which Ruben Love has seized his opportunity this year that his starting spot never really felt under pressure from either Beauden Barrett or Richie Mo'unga – at this stage at least. Ellis Park and the world champions will ratchet the pressure up another notch for the young fly half, but he has looked totally assured in his first tastes of Test rugby.

Where can he hurt the Springboks? Certainly, the territorial kicking game will be vital. With Jordie Barrett and Damian McKenzie in the side as well, New Zealand can vary their first receiver to create both opportunities in attack and at finding backfield space. South Africa's aggressive blitz defence can leave spaces on the edges at times, too: look for Love to try and target Josh Moorby and Will Jordan – two solid aerial operators with comfort playing at full-back – in the spaces between the hosts' wings and Damian Willemse.

What luxury it must be for South Africa to name a player like Esterhuizen on their bench and essentially get two for the price of one with his ability to cover the flank and centres. The hybridisation trend of 2025 saw a number of nations experiment with individuals who can play in the forwards and backs, and New Zealand might have unleashed one of their own in Leicester Fainga'anuku if not for an ill-timed injury for the wing-cum-centre-cum-flanker.

Esterhuizen, though, was operating at an extremely high level in his dual role last year. His introduction in Wellington, which came at inside centre, when these two last met transformed the complexion of that encounter, though it may be that he is required in the back row at some stage here.

It feels telling that South Africa have plumped for their best scrummaging props in Ox Nche, fit again after injury, and Wilco Louw. New Zealand have looked a little vulnerable in that area in their tour matches, though Ethan de Groot and Tyrel Lomax are more than capable of holding their own, and have a strong set-piece hooker in Codie Taylor between them.

The trio lasted 66 minutes in the World Cup final, which proved crucial to securing parity up front. They may have to go that deep again – and at the lung-sapping altitude of 1,753 metres up on the Highveld.

title: Is Arsenal vs Coventry on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Premier League season opener
description: Everything you need to know as the 2026/27 Premier League season gets underway
fullText:
The Premier League is back, with reigning champions Arsenal beginning their title defence against last year's Championship winners Coventry City.

Frank Lampard's side have the toughest possible task to kick off their return to the top flight for the first time in over two decades, particularly as the Gunners looked so impressive as they cruised to a 3-0 Community Shield win over a dispirited Manchester City side in their last outing.

Both sides have strengthened in the transfer window, although Coventry have hardly spent big - particularly in comparison to Mikel Arteta's side, who have brought in ex-Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis as well as securing the services of Piero Hincapie permanently after a loan spell last year.

These two sides are expected to finish at opposite ends of the table but Coventry will relish the challenge against the hot favourites for the title, while after that long-awaited title the current iteration of Arsenal will aim to prove they aren't one-hit wonders.

Here's everything you need to know.

Arsenal host Coventry at the Emirates Stadium on Friday 21 August, with kick-off at 8pm BST.

Viewers in the UK can watch the match on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League. If you're not a Sky customer, you can grab a NOWTV Day Pass here to watch without a subscription.

Arsenal will be missing William Saliba and Jurrien Timber through injury, while Arteta has a dilemma on his hands over whether to start Bukayo saka and Declan Rice, who are working back to full fitness after lengthy campaigns last term and at the World Cup.

Coventry will be without the injured Haji Wright and Luke Woolfenden, with Jack Rudoni and Frank Onyeka also doubts.

Arsenal XI: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly, Guimaraes, Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis, Havertz

Coventry XI: Rushworth, Van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Markelo, Onyeka, Grimes, Yirenkyi, Tchaouna, Simms, Thomas-Asante

title: Max Verstappen, a record-breaking Red Bull stay and a show of faith in Formula 1
description: COMMENT: Verstappen has extended his contract with Red Bull until 2030 but, as Kieran Jackson explains, the real news is the Dutchman has opted to stay in Formula 1 for the foreseeable future – when a shock retirement seemed very plausible
fullText:
In the space of six months, it has been some turnaround. The first time Max Verstappen drove the much-maligned, energy-dependent breed of 2026 Formula 1 car at February testing in Bahrain, his response was apoplectic. "Anti-racing" and "like Formula E on steroids" were two such protestations. Six weeks on, after round three at one of Formula 1's staple high-speed circuits, Suzuka in Japan, the Dutchman's disgruntlement had reached boiling point. Quitting the sport seemed a real eventuality.

"It's really anti-driving," Verstappen told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Then at one point, yeah, it's just not what I want to do. And of course you can look at it and make a lot of money. Great. But at the end of the day it's not about money any more because this has always been my passion."

Yet behind the scenes, conversations and proposals moved quickly. Highly-respected F1 chief executive Stefano Domenicali held cordial talks with Verstappen while the Dutchman's long-term manager, Raymond Vermeulen, spoke to McLaren boss Zak Brown. Verstappen's outspoken father and former driver, Jos, was also seen in conversation with Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff in Canada. Team Verstappen were plotting their next move.

Yet all the while, the biggest turning point came in May, when F1 announced changes to the sport's controversial engine regulations, with traditional energy power increased and the energy recovery system decreased for 2027. Further afield, there is a genuine push from FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem for a return to the ear-splitting V8 engines (last seen in 2008 to 2013) for the next regulations cycle in 2030.

No wonder, then, that Verstappen's fresh Red Bull extension – with improved terms beyond his previous £60m-a-year deal – is until that very year.

"From my side, I adapted and accepted the situation that we're all in," Verstappen said on Thursday, at a packed media conference in Red Bull's "Energy Station" motorhome at his home circuit in Zandvoort, hosting Formula 1 for the last time this weekend.

"I'm just trying to make the best of that. With the year that I signed to [2030], it again opens up the door, maybe, when potentially the V8s come in, to look at that again as well."

Verstappen's new contract, kept impressively under wraps at the team's Milton Keynes HQ over the last 48 hours, is more a show of faith in Formula 1 than it is in Red Bull. It is a team he has represented for 11 consecutive seasons now – the 28-year-old is now set to break the F1 record for a driver-team partnership, currently held by Lewis Hamilton and Mercedes' dozen years together – and now looks set to see out his career with.

Despite his trusted race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase joining McLaren as Head of Racing, either next year or in 2028, and summer encounters in Sardinia with Wolff and his family, an under-emphasised characteristic of Verstappen's irrepressible on-track hunger is his loyalty: to his people, to his team and to the brand. For team principal Laurent Mekies – a year on from taking over as Christian Horner's replacement – it is the biggest of boosts heading into the second half of the season.

"I was closer to retiring than changing teams," Verstappen said. "I like it here. I think it would be a great story if that were possible, being picked up by Red Bull and finishing your career with one team.

"I don't feel the need to change just to change… after the first few races [this season], I said to Laurent, 'Don't come to me with any kind of questions about the future because I didn't even know if I want to stay'.

"But honestly, we always kept it very open. I love racing, and I had a lot of very good discussions with F1, but also with the FIA. We are slowly working towards something that becomes better and better."

There is also an underlying sense at Red Bull that, despite high-profile technical exits in recent years (as well as Horner, design genius Adrian Newey, pit-stop guru Jonathan Wheatley and strategy chief Will Courtenay have all departed), the team have plenty of unfulfilled potential in this current regulation cycle.

Building their own engine for the first time this season, in partnership with Ford, Red Bull were statistically named the strongest power unit in the spring, in spite of Mercedes' supposed dominance. That represents plenty of room for development in a chassis which both Verstappen and teammate Isack Hadjar have struggled to contend with in the opening 11 rounds.

Regardless, it is a suspicious time for Verstappen to commit, ahead of 12 races in 16 weeks to conclude the current campaign. Despite four very respectable podiums, Verstappen is currently on course for his first winless season since his rookie campaign with sister team Toro Rosso in 2015. Yet here he is, a four-time world champion, who could probably land any seat on the grid if he opted to forcefully abandon ship, committing for the foreseeable future with the only team he's ever known.

In similar circumstances two years ago, Hamilton opted for a final swansong move to the prancing horse of Ferrari. Verstappen, however, has stayed put, perhaps in the knowledge that great times are ahead for Red Bull once more. Yet there will be performance clauses; there will be exit stipulations. The penning of fresh papers silences the noise for now. But only Red Bull's on-track performance will quieten the doubters in the long run.

title: How to watch Vuelta a Espana 2026: TV channel, highlights and streaming online
description: All you need to know about how to watch this year’s Vuelta a Espana
fullText:
The final Grand Tour of the year is on the horizon as the peloton gathers in Monaco for the start of the Vuelta a Espana.

Defending champion Jonas Vingegaard will not take to the start line after winning the Giro d'Italia this spring before crashing and breaking his collarbone at the Tour de France last month.

But his great rival Tadej Pogacar - seemingly not content with the Dane completing the trio of grand tour victories before him - is the headline name as he returns to the Vuelta for the first time in seven years, after he finished third, winning three stages and the best young rider's classification, in 2019.

The two-time world champion is, as always, the overwhelming favourite, even after his exploits winning a record-equalling fifth Tour de France this summer, while his UAE Team Emirates-XRG outfit have enough quality to complete a podium sweep, with Joao Almeida and Jay Vine in tow as super-domestiques.

Away from the general classification battle British starlet Matthew Brennan has been selected for his first grand tour, while the evenly-matched Wout van Aert and Mads Pedersen are likely to do battle for the points jersey.

Here's everything you need to know to watch the race.

The Vuelta a Espana runs for 21 stages plus two rest days from 22 August to 13 September 2026, beginning in Monaco and finishing in Granada.

Viewers in the UK can watch the Vuelta a Espana on TNT Sports and streaming service HBO Max. Free-to-air highlights will be available on DMAX.

Stage 1 (August 22): Monaco to Monaco: Time trial (9.4km)

Stage 2 (August 23): Monaco to Manosque (France): Hilly stage (214.3km)

Stage 3 (August 24): Gruissan to Font-Romeu: Medium mountain stage (174km)

Stage 4 (August 25): Andorra la Vella to Andorra la Vella: Mountain stage (104.8km)

Stage 5 (August 26): Falset to Roquetes: Hilly stage (173.4km)

Stage 6 (August 27): Alcossebre to Castelló: Medium mountain stage (177.4km)

Stage 7 (August 28): Vall d'Alba to Aramón Valdelinares: Mountain stage (149.8km)

Stage 8 (August 29): Puçol to Xeraco: Flat stage (171km)

Stage 9 (August 30): La Vila Joiosa to Alto de Aitana: Mountain stage (187.4km)

Stage 10 (September 1): Alcaraz to Elche de la Sierra: Hilly stage (184.7km)

Stage 11 (September 2): Cartagena to Lorca: Flat stage (151.3km)

Stage 12 (September 3): Vera to Calar Alto: Mountain stage (166.6km)

Stage 13 (September 4): Almuñécar to Loja: Medium mountain stage (192.8km)

title: Tadej Pogacar will win the Vuelta a Espana. Here’s why you should still watch it
description: IN DEPTH: It feels inevitable Pogacar will complete the grand tour set, Flo Clifford writes, but there remains plenty that is harder to predict about what should still be a fascinating edition of La Vuelta
fullText:
Barring calamity, Tadej Pogacar will be standing on the podium in Granada in three weeks' time clad in red. The Slovenian supremo is returning to the only grand tour he has yet to win for the first time in seven years. It was at this race in 2019 where he burst onto the scene, finishing third overall and winning three stages as well as the best young rider's jersey, with compatriot Primoz Roglic winning the first of his four titles.

Decathlon CMA CGM's Felix Gall, second at the Giro, is well suited to the climbs but will lose minutes against the clock; Roglic is back but at 36 is in the twilight of his career, and his preparation will not have been helped by being hit by a car in training three weeks ago.

Surprises do happen and nothing is certain in three-week racing; Jonas Vingegaard rarely crashes but was forced to abandon this year's Tour and then end his season early after breaking his collarbone. But it would take an unprecedented collapse or serious misfortune to deny Pogacar the maillot rojo.

What hope for his rivals, then? Much of this year's route is concentrated in southern Spain, where sweltering late summer temperatures might expose vulnerabilities within UAE Team Emirates-XRG, although – having worked on what was once a weakness, punished in his two Tour defeats to Vingegaard – the heat is unlikely to be such an issue for Pogacar.

Alternatively he may have the Vuelta wrapped up by the end of the first week and concentrate on helping his lieutenants, possibly to complete a clean sweep of the podium, as arch-rivals Visma-Lease a Bike managed at this race in 2023. The luckless Jay Vine is back after crashing out early in the Giro d'Italia, and Joao Almeida is riding his first grand tour of the season after an underwhelming campaign for a rider of his undisputed quality. So the story of the Vuelta may instead be Pogacar as an unlikely Samaritan, shepherding his teammates to glory of their own.

But if the 27-year-old's pursuit of yet more greatness, and a seemingly inevitable title, leaves some viewers cold, there is plenty else to follow at the year's most unpredictable grand tour.

The most exciting battle of this year's Tour was between Mads Pedersen and Jasper Philipsen for the green points jersey, and the points classification should be a thrilling watch in Spain too as Pedersen returns, this time in a duel with Wout van Aert.

Visma-Lease a Bike are fielding a mixed squad which includes 2023 Vuelta winner Sepp Kuss, but the American has always been more of a climber than an outright GC rider despite that win, so the Belgian leads their squad. He and Pedersen lit up the spring – who could forget Van Aert winning an all-time classic edition of Paris-Roubaix against Pogacar – and the resumption of their rivalry is eagerly anticipated.

Visma have another card to play as they hand a grand tour debut to British talent Matthew Brennan, who was single-handedly responsible for a quarter of the entire team's wins last season. The 21-year-old's winning percentage has not been as ludicrous this year, but he did win Kuurne-Brussels-Kuurne and two stages of the Vuelta a Burgos earlier this month, so arrives in sparkling form.

Another Briton to watch is Oscar Onley. The 23-year-old has had a difficult first season as the face of Netcompany-Ineos' grand tour hopes, having been stymied by injury at seemingly every turn and openly frustrated at himself, writing on social media after an abandon earlier this year that it was "hard not to feel like I've let a lot of people down". A significant shoulder injury ruled him out of the Tour de France, where he finished an exceptional fourth last year, but he has returned in form and motivated, finishing second overall and winning a stage in Burgos.

This Vuelta a Espana will be his first grand tour riding in Netcompany-Ineos colours and feels a pivotal point already in his young career: instructive both of what he can do with a strong team around him, and of whether the British-Danish outfit has realistic ambitions of being a grand tour power once again, particularly after an entirely anonymous Tour.

It goes without saying that this Vuelta will be raced under a huge cloud as the peloton reels from the death of 19-year-old Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal. Tarling collided with a non-race vehicle which was not prevented from getting onto the course, sparking widespread outrage at the lack of security at the race alongside an outpouring of grief for a talented, popular young rider.

The accident is under investigation by Portuguese police. While racing continues, security and rider safety will be under forensic scrutiny. Last year's Vuelta was marred by repeated protests which occasionally turned ugly and put riders at risk. That is unlikely to be a problem this time around after the rebranding of Israel-PremierTech, the target of much ire, late last season. But the issue of how organisers and police keep riders from harm will remain, justifiably, under the spotlight.

Ineos were the last team to announce their roster for the race, waiting until two days prior to the start in Monaco, to give Tarling's brother Josh as much time as possible to decide whether to race or not. The announcement that the 22-year-old would take part was accompanied by a note Geraint Thomas, Ineos' director of racing: "It also goes without saying that, as a team, we all fully support Josh in his decision to take part in the race."

To have the strength to ride is awe-inspiring. Results, of course, are secondary at a time like this, and there should be no expectation placed on his young shoulders. But Tarling has a significant opportunity to take the leader's jersey in the opening day time trial – a result which the entire cycling community will surely wish for.

title: The Premier League is entering a different era – and 11 new managers show us why
description: PREMIER LEAGUE PREVIEW: A summer of change has left new faces in charge of most of England’s biggest clubs – leaving, Miguel Delaney writes, both uncertainty and opportunity
fullText:
At Chelsea's Cobham training ground, players have already remarked on one way that Xabi Alonso has lived up to his reputation. The training sessions rarely follow a set pattern, ensuring the squad have to think about everything a lot more. They're kept on their toes, if not to the same degree that Liverpool are. Andoni Iraola has his new group adapting to different "physiological demands". There's been a jolt.

At Newcastle United, Matthias Jaissle may not have such a reputation, but he's had a similar effect. People have already been impressed, to the point of perceived "sacrilege". Many are talking about how the coaching is a higher quality than Eddie Howe.

If Howe had long been seen as a "next England manager", Jaissle is genuinely viewed as "the next big coach".

And despite such disparate situations across the Premier League, there is a link here, especially when you look back to the obvious contrast of the summer of 2016.

Then, when Pep Guardiola was arriving rather than going, the Premier League really wasn't about the next big names.

It was about the biggest right then, as Guardiola joined Jurgen Klopp, Jose Mourinho, Antonio Conte, Arsene Wenger and Mauricio Pochettino.

The Premier League became the "league of star managers", a status that fit England's grand history of managerial patriarchs.

The lack of such names now is all the more notable amid a debate about the lack of "star players", since a longer lineage has been broken.

This is the first Premier League season with none of Ferguson, Wenger, Mourinho or Guardiola involved. In other words, the great title-winning totems.

Mikel Arteta is in fact the only current coach to have even won the English league at all, having just claimed his first.

That victory came out of "almost complete control" at Arsenal, a level of command that emulates those "big beasts" of the past, as they were called, and is increasingly rare in the modern game.

That it's Arteta may be all the more apt since he does fit into one theme that has been discussed in the same way as 2016's stars.

If that was about the biggest names, this is about Basque names.

The one piece of discourse you've probably seen more this pre-season than Alonso's superior technique in training is discussion of how the Chelsea boss is one of three coaches – along with Iraola and Arteta – to come from the same team in Antiguoko, to go with how Unai Emery also hails from the same region around San Sebastian.

If it's obvious to say this is immensely impressive overrepresentation for such a small area, it is equally unfashionable to state some of it is possibly just coincidence. This has happened in numerous cities in various fields throughout history, and you don't have to go as high-brow as Vienna and its nucleus composers. Just consider the great documentaries made on how Glasgow's industrial hardships produced Jock Stein, Sir Matt Busby and Bill Shankly all at the same time, and eventually Ferguson.

The freakish coincidence of producing coaches of such high quality can still be connected to wider cultural forces, though. The Basque country shares Spain's wider football ideology, with Salamanca-born Alvaro Arbeloa now sharing a place in the Premier League. His first Fulham match comes against former teammate Alonso, on Monday.

English inquests are warranted at how a quarter of the Premier League's managers are Spanish at the same time as Spain are reigning European and world champions, with their national team having displayed a depth of tactical sophistication that England couldn't get close to. England actually seem so far away they had to opt for another big-name coach in Thomas Tuchel, at the expense of a figure like Howe.

The country may be the home of the vintage managerial patriarch but it is not currently a hot house for elite modern coaches. Something has been missing, despite brilliant talent production with players.

And it is within that gap that the most telling link between this season's managers lies.

More relevant than a fifth of the coaches being Basque is how two of those are among nine managers new to their jobs.

More than half of the Premier League – including Michael Carrick and Roberto De Zerbi, taking it to 11 – are currently working through their first pre-seasons with these teams. The 33-year-old Fabian Hurzeler is meanwhile the joint-fourth longest serving coach, with newly-appointed Marco Rose the 12th.

Such statistics from quite a contrast to 10 years ago, when it was all about stature and legacy.

Against the 28 titles that eight managers had won across eight different countries in 2016, only five of the current group have won titles – and four of those seven came in Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia.

Outside Arteta, only Emery and Alonso have experience of winning a major league.

Sergej Jakirovic (Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatian Football League)

Matthias Jaissle (Austrian Bundesliga x2)

Some in football have been talking about a group of "unknowns" and "randoms" set for multiple sackings, evidently ignoring the instructive example of Pochettino's Southampton appointment back in 2013.

And that is where there is a spin on this akin to an especially creative training drill.

The current crop may not have anything near the recognition of 2016, but numerous more people in football are adamant the Premier League is now collectively much better coached.

This is just what the competition is now, with years of broadcasting wealth gradually ensuring almost all clubs have properly invested in their football intelligence. They're simply hiring the brightest.

And if the short time spans of these managers also speaks to the grand theme of last season, and the increasing influence of directors and executives, it similarly reflects the speed at which all of this is evolving. This is now a fast-moving game, to go with how it is defined by physical intensity.

Clubs now actively prefer low-maintenance managers who will concentrate on the coaching, of which Iraola is a rare ideal. An irony is that successful management often necessitates stronger personalities, but that also plays into an intense concentration on the coaching.

Long-time football figures have been blown away by this.

Relatively standard practice now is coaches working from 6am to well into the night, with new plans presented every single morning. The manager will then ensure every cone is in its exact place so everything can be executed to the essential level, with all of this then pored over for hours on video afterwards.

It's been written on these pages before that pressing systems are so sophisticated that they form the unseen map that shapes matches, normally nurtured by drill programmes that even have the positions of water bottles marked out.

In other words, the obsessiveness that elevated Guardiola is now commonplace.

Little wonder coaches talk of the most competitive Premier League ever, due to how much everyone has to think and prepare. This constant battle for space is partly why there's been an inevitable devolution into wrestling matches for space at set-pieces.

The neural networks that all of this forms – a little like, say, Vienna in the 1700s – have at least ensured that football tactics, certainly at a micro level, are constantly evolving faster than ever.

As an illustration, Alonso's core ideas were seen as brilliantly innovative five years ago but a lot of the Premier League have now taken those even further. It's just as well he's so good as a pure manager. That is another constant challenge, though, that Arteta is known to be obsessed with. You don't just have to think about your own team's coaching all the time, but whether you yourself are keeping pace with all of the most advanced ideas.

As one club insider says, the game has just changed so much from even three to four years ago.

And that's almost a completely different world to 10 years ago.

It's not about the big names. It's about greater ideas, executed to the most granular level.

title: Lakers Insider Offers Major Nikola Jokic Trade Update Amid Ownership Change
description: The Los Angeles Lakers will reportedly turn their attention to the long-rumored Nikola Jokic trade after their ownership change. The post Lakers Insider Offers Major Nikola Jokic Trade Update Amid Ownership Change appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Lakers will reportedly turn their attention to the long-rumored Nikola Jokic trade once their new ownership takes charge of the franchise.

According to Lakers insider Anthony Irwin, the franchise's eyes are going to be "dead-set" on the Denver Nuggets once their ownership situation is figured out.

"All I'll say is if/when the Lakers get their ownership situation figured out, a lot of the organization's eyes are going to be dead-set on Denver," Irwin reported via X.

Hypothetically, the Lakers could build a package around Walker Kessler and/or Austin Reaves, but none of those trades will be possible until Jan. 15, 2027, when the trade restrictions on both players will expire. While Kessler inked a 4-year, $130M contract with the Lakers via a sign-and-trade this offseason, Reaves signed a four-year, $184M to stay with the franchise that took a chance on him after he went undrafted in 2021.

For what it's worth Jokic, who has the option to test free agency in 2027, has repeatedly stated his desire to re-sign with the Nuggets next summer.

"My idea and desire is to stay in Denver. I'll probably sign next year," he said last month after a FIBA World Cup qualifier game.

"… My desire is to play the rest of my life in Denver."

The chatter of Jokic potentially leaving Denver gathered steam after the three-time MVP turned down a four-year, $278 extension this summer. However, ESPN's Dave McMenamin explained that there was a strategic reason for Jokic to not re-up this year, as he's eligible for an additional $80M if he waits until 2027.

"By waiting until the 2027 offseason, Jokic is eligible to sign a five-year $359.5 million contract as a free agent," McMenamin reported last month. "That contract would be the largest in NBA history and would see his career on-court earnings reach $724 million, according to ESPN NBA front office insider Bobby Marks."

Despite Jokic's insistence to remain in Denver, several insiders have highlighted that Giannis Antetokounmpo maintained a similar, loyal stance with the Milwaukee Bucks before finally seeking a trade this past summer.

As such, there's no guarantee that Jokic won't have a similar change of heart, especially if the Nuggets continue to underwhelm in the playoffs. Notably, the Nuggets have failed to advance past the second round of the playoffs since their title win in 2023 — in large part due to their unwillingness to pay their free agents. Most recently, they let Peyton Watson walk to shed at least $100M off their pay roll for next year.

Former Nuggets coach George Karl has warned that the franchise risks losing Jokic due to some of its front-office decisions in recent years.

"Some franchises aren't capable of supporting their legends the right way.

"Jokic was on a path to becoming one of the Top 10 players to ever play basketball.

"That wasn't realistic in Denver," Karl wrote on X on Thursday.

title: The Manchester City rebuild is continuing as evidenced by what has occurred this week
description: The documentary ‘A Beautiful Obsession’ was released in the UK and Ireland on Amazon Prime earlier this week. Kevin MacDonald’s brilliant documentary provides a behind-the-scenes look at the fin...
fullText:
The documentary 'A Beautiful Obsession' was released in the UK and Ireland on Amazon Prime earlier this week. Kevin MacDonald's brilliant documentary provides a behind-the-scenes look at the final two seasons of Pep Guardiola's decade-long tenure as Manchester City manager. The documentary is powerful and filled with standout moments which show the emotion that Guardiola, Manchester City the club, the players, and departing legends experienced over the past two seasons. Also, the documentary shows how City have gone about their rebuild after Guardiola's decade of dominance. That process is continuing this summer and based on which players have left the club and could leave the club it isn't an exact science and there will be some missteps along the way.

The January 2025 transfer window was when the Manchester City rebuild fully began. City didn't make the necessary signings in the summer of 2024 and had to get bodies into Pep Guardiola's squad as Manchester City's 2024-25 season fell apart. During the January 2025 transfer window, City signed Omar Marmoush, Nico Gonzalez, Vitor Reis, Abdukodir Khusanov, Juma Bah and Christian McFarlane. The signings of Bah and McFarlane were youth signings and aren't relevant to the topic at hand. Savinho was also signed by City in the summer of 2024 alongside Ilkay Gundogan.

Of that group, only Abdukodir Khusanov has established himself as a valuable player for the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders. The jury remains out on Vitor Reis. Omar Marmoush, Nico Gonzalez, and Savinho could all leave City this summer. Savinho is on the verge of getting his coveted move to Tottenham. Marmoush may follow him to Spurs and Nico Gonzalez's future is uncertain.

Marmoush, Savinho, and Nico Gonzalez are three players would go down as players that City have signed that haven't had the desired results. They have had their moments, but haven't come on as expected. That is why they're all likely to depart. Tijjani Reijnders was a summer 2025 signing and he has also left Manchester City after one season at the club. His departure also shows that City are still searching for the right players to take the club forward or complement the core they already have.

The fact that Manchester City could make a profit on players that haven't made the required impact does arm them to bolster Enzo Maresca's squad. That is the step that City have to get right.

Manchester City enter the final two weeks of this summer's transfer window needing to make four, potentially five, signings to bolster Enzo Maresca's squad. These are moves in the transfer market that City cannot afford to miss on. If Omar Marmoush, Nico Gonzalez, Savinho, and Tijjani Reijnders had made the necessary impact they all wouldn't be considered likely to leave City or have left the club already. This is the situation that City are in. But that isn't the entire situation.

Bernardo Silva, Rodri, John Stones and Nathan Ake have all departed City. As has James Trafford. Manchester City signed Gerónimo Rulli to be Gianluigi Donnarumma's backup. The fact that a core group of leaders and key players have left, alongside the potential departures of a host of squad players means Manchester City have to shop at the top-shelf over the next two weeks. They have no other option.

Manchester City's rebuild after their era of dominance is continuing. Not all of the signings that City have made since the January 2025 transfer window have hit the mark. Also, a host of important players at the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders have departed. What Manchester City need now is obvious; they need to find players who can come in now and raise the ceiling of their squad. They now have under two weeks to sign them. But the situation Manchester City are facing now shows that Manchester City's rebuild remains a work in progress and could be that for some time if they don't nail their signings before the transfer window closes.

title: Crystal Palace look to have squashed any chance of Manchester City signing an England international
description: Manchester City continues to search for midfielders that they can sign to bolster Enzo Maresca’s squad. Crystal Palace’s England international Adam Wharton was named as a potential target for the ...
fullText:
Manchester City continues to search for midfielders that they can sign to bolster Enzo Maresca's squad. Crystal Palace's England international Adam Wharton was named as a potential target for the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders. Wharton's passing game and quality in possession seem suited to life in a City side. It has now been reported that Manchester City have enquired about the possibility of signing Adam Wharton. However, Crystal Palace appear to have quickly squashed City's hopes of signing Wharton.

David Ornstein and Sam Lee have reported for The Athletic that Manchester City have enquired with Crystal Palace about the potential of signing Adam Wharton this summer. However, Crystal Palace have informed City that they have no intention of selling Wharton this summer. It is also reported that Wharton is one of many candidates City have on their recruitment list. However, the name of those players isn't revealed.

Manchester City are now in a race against time to bolster their squad ahead of the transfer window closing. My personal belief is that City wouldn't be willing to let so many players depart without having a plan in place. That plan is yet to properly reveal itself. However, due to the stage of the transfer window where City are trying to do major work, they may face frustration or be forced to pay a premium.

Crystal Palace's stance on not wanting to sell Adam Wharton is understandable. They will not want to lose such an important player so late in the transfer window. Unless Wharton attempts to engineer an exit from Crystal Palace late in the window, which looks unlikely, City will have to look elsewhere to bolster their midfield. This is a scenario that could be in play for a host of clubs who will not want to lose key players without having the time to sign a replacement. The other possibility is that Manchester City will have to pay a premium to sign players so late in the window which is now a likely scenario which will take place.

Adam Wharton looks set to stay at Crystal Palace. Manchester City's enquiry about signing the England international has been dismissed. City's hunt for quality midfielders continues and it will be a process that will likely drag on until the final day of the transfer window.

title: Barcelona agree personal terms with Julian Alvarez alternative; deal still difficult – report
description: Barcelona’s search for a new striker appears to have taken an important step forward, with the Catalan giants reportedly reaching an agreement with Lautaro Martinez over personal terms.The problem, ...
fullText:
Barcelona's search for a new striker appears to have taken an important step forward, with the Catalan giants reportedly reaching an agreement with Lautaro Martinez over personal terms.

The problem, however, is that agreeing terms with the player is only one part of the equation.

As reported before, Barcelona have not yet made an offer to Inter Milan, and the Serie A side is not currently expecting one.

More significantly, Inter are said to have no interest in opening talks for their captain, creating a major obstacle in any potential Lautaro Martinez transfer.

With Julian Alvarez increasingly difficult to sign, Barcelona have been forced to look at other options, and Lautaro has emerged as one of the names being seriously considered.

Barcelona's striker plans have changed considerably following the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, leaving the club with a significant gap in the final third.

Lautaro Martinez has agreed personal terms with Barcelona. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Finding a player capable of replacing that experience and goal output was always going to be difficult, particularly with Barcelona's financial situation and the prices attached to the world's leading forwards.

Alvarez had been viewed as an attractive option, but a move for the Argentine has reportedly become close to impossible.

That development has pushed Barcelona to consider alternatives, with Lautaro Martinez becoming a serious target.

According to El Chiringuito TV, Barcelona sporting director Deco and Bojan Krkic met Lautaro's representative in Madrid last week.

The report claims those talks resulted in an agreement with the player over personal terms.

The financial conditions of a potential contract have already been discussed, meaning Barcelona could move on the player's side if they ever manage to reach an agreement with Inter Milan.

Inter Milan will not sell Lautaro Martinez. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

The bigger issue is Inter Milan.

The Italian side has received no official Barcelona offer for Lautaro Martinez, and their position suggests they would not be interested in negotiating even if one arrived.

Lautaro is not just another important player in the Inter squad; he is the club captain, a leader in the dressing room and one of their most reliable goalscorers.

Inter also hold a strong position because the Argentine striker is tied to the club until 2029, meaning Barcelona would need to overcome both Inter's resistance and what could be a substantial transfer fee.

From the player's perspective, Lautaro is excited by the possibility of playing for Barcelona, despite being happy in Milan and fully committed to his current role with Inter.

But at this stage, there is still a huge difference between Barcelona agreeing terms with a player and Barcelona actually completing a deal.

title: What channel is Steelers vs. Jets on today? Time, TV schedule, live stream to watch NFL Week 2 preseason game

title: Deion Sanders finds himself on the wrong coaching list for 2026
description: Coach Prime’s roster overhaul at Colorado sparks fears that his rebuilding strategy won't yield wins.
fullText:
The Colorado Buffaloes are in the middle of one of two things right now. A complete culture shift or a gentleman's rebuild.

The program's messaging this offseason has suggested this is a pendulum effect after a 3-9 season when players failed to meet the moment. Several of those players were highly rated and big NIL earners. All gone, with many replaced with lower ranked players from lower competition levels.

The other option is a gentlemen's rebuild. A concept usually reserved for the NFL. When a team finds themselves on the downward swing with an expensive or aging team, one option is a full, tear it down to the studs rebuild. Or, more popular as of late, a gentlemen's rebuild.

That concept would include shedding all your high-priced talent by way of a trade or being released. Those players are replaced with cheaper options, preferably players who are productive but likely on their final pro contract. Then trade back in the draft and acquire future assets. In 1-3 years, this approach allows a team to reset the financials and take big swings. Creating what seems like a dramatic turnaround in only a couple of years instead of four years or more.

The concern with the culture shift is that there is very little data to show that approach works in college football. Getting the biggest, best, most highly rated talent has always created the best chance to win. Curt Cignetti did it with Indiana last year, but as we are starting to learn, Cignetti is maybe the greatest outlier in recent memory.

If it is a gentleman's rebuild, it would make sense. The University of Colorado self-reported a $27M deficit heading into this fiscal year. In the NIL era, it makes it very difficult to pay players hundreds of thousands, if not millions, and you're over $20M in the hole. Shedding those high-priced players would change the financial equation to some degree. However, the elephant in the room is that Deion Sanders might not have the 1-3 years afforded to a gentleman's rebuild.

The Buffs need to win. This season. To reach even .500 at Colorado, Sanders needs nine wins this season. The hype behind Colorado in 2023 and 2024 has all but completely faded. According to Michael McCarthy of Front Office Sports, television ratings for Colorado games broadcast on ESPN have fallen by 67%. After almost reaching double-digit wins and a Heisman Trophy winner, the Buffs had an objectively bad showing in the Alamo Bowl vs BYU. Almost everything that followed was below expectations.

A revolving door at quarterback. Four running backs that did not add up to 1,000 yards total. Only one receiver that put up threatening numbers. A defense that did not boast a single player with 60 tackles or more. For context, there were 417 players with 60 or more tackles last season according to ESPN. The top five pass rushers registered less than 10 sacks combined. After 2024 when they led the conference in that metric.

A 1-8 record against Big 12 opponents. Zero wins on the road. 0-5 to end the season. 20.9 points per game, which was good for 116th in the FBS. An offensive line that gave up 38 sacks. While that is far cry from the 56 allowed in 2023, it still is only good enough to rank 125th nationally.

On Monday, Yahoo Sports released a list of 10 college football coaches under the most pressure in 2026. A hot seat list is not uncommon just before the start of the season. However, this year's list is not one Coach Prime wants to be on if they aim to significantly change the narratives surrounding the Buffaloes.

There are only two names on this list, not counting Sanders, whose star power and recent results could protect them if 2026 is not great. Kalen DeBoer and Lincoln Riley. DeBoer and Alabama finished second in the SEC with 11 wins and just barely missed the college football playoff. Riley is a little more troubling, finishing 5th in the Big Ten and was certainly on the outside looking in. However, Riley is still viewed as a potential genius level offensive mind.

Every other name on this list could be viewed as needing a "great" season to keep the vultures away. Dave Aranda at Baylor, Shane Beamer at South Carolina, Bill Belichick at North Carolina, Luke Fickell at Wisconsin, Mike Locksley at Maryland, Mike Norvell at Florida State and even Dabo Swinney at Clemson were all expected to be fired at some point in the 2025 college football season.

Seven of the ten were dangerously close to getting fired. Two of the ten have a name or program that could save them. The other name is Deion Sanders. Of the ten names on the Yahoo list, only one team has dramatically changed their player acquisition process. Only one team got rid of most of their perceived top talent. Only one team is betting on the hunger of under-recruited players to beat teams full of 4-and 5-star players. That team is Colorado.

There could be a reality where the Buffaloes are successful this season. After a 3-9 campaign, though, they would certainly need to be a bowl-eligible team at minimum, to call this season a success. Getting Coach Prime completely off the hot seat would almost require nine wins or more.

title: Fabrizio Romano confirms two forwards coming when Gakpo is sold
description: Liverpool’s long-stated aim in this summer’s transfer window is adding one-v-one quality out wide. The plan was to add Yan Diomande but after RB Leipzig knocked back the Reds’ bid the Ivorian 19...
fullText:
Liverpool's long-stated aim in this summer's transfer window is adding one-v-one quality out wide.

The plan was to add Yan Diomande but after RB Leipzig knocked back the Reds' bid the Ivorian 19-year-old joined Real Madrid instead.

Since then the focus has been on bringing in Bradley Barcola. It's proving to be a tricky task indeed however with Paris Saint-Germain intending to ask for £145m before letting the 23-year-old go.

Separately to the deal for Barcola it is believed that Liverpool are also chasing a move for Ibrahim Mbaye. The 18-year-old - a PSG teammate of Barcola - woud come in significantly cheaper but he is a far lesser proven player than the France international.

An added complication is that Richard Hughes has already spent around £100m in this summer's transfer window so far. Victor Munoz has been onboarded for £34m from Osasuna and Jeremy Jacquet came in for £60m from Rennes.

Ronald Araujo has been brought in on loan with a significant pay packet - meaning money is at a premium for the Merseysiders.

Sales will mean added spending money with Curtis Jones putting £30m in the cash register upon his sale to Inter Milan.

And one other solution could be to sell Cody Gakpo to Tottenham. The Dutchman, 27, inked a new contract deal last year worth around £250k per week - tying him to the club until 2030.

That means Liverpool are quite well protected from a transfer fee perspective and a deal to take the Netherlands forward to North London has been estimated at around £60m.

Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that a deal for Gakpo to go to Spurs is still alive - adding that the versatile forward's exit would mean TWO extra wideman coming into Anfield this summer.

"For Cody Gakpo, Tottenham remain in conversations," he tells his YouTube audience.

"I know in the last 24, 48 hours, the rumours around the story are that the deal is not happening, the deal is off, the deal is not going through.

"But my understanding is that the negotiation for Cody Gakpo to Tottenham is still ongoing. Cody Gakpo is open to joining Tottenham and personal terms are not a problem.

"So the deal remains on. The deal remains underway and Cody Gakpo to Tottenham Hotspur is still absolutely on.

"Then they need to reach a financial agreement, and that's not a detail. Remember that if Gakpo is going to Tottenham, Liverpool will sign two wingers, top target Bradley Barcola plus one.

"So it's still a long story in a short time because now there are less than two weeks of the summer transfer window. We'll be following the situation. These days, anything can happen.

"But what I can guarantee at this time on Tuesday is that nothing has changed yet. There is no deal off. The conversation remains ongoing and we have to follow the situation to understand what's going to happen."

It's believed Iraola would like to have five winger options at his disposal this season. Munoz and Rio Ngumoha are locked in with Federico Chiesa's place in the squad in doubt amid interest from elsewhere.

Gakpo leaving the club would spark two more signings - Barcola and perhaps Mbaye or else Yankuba Minteh from Brighton. That in turn would leave one place up for grabs with Lewis Koumas likely to be offered increased first-team minutes this season.

title: Premier League 2026/27 matchday 1 predictions: New era beckons as Newcastle vs Liverpool headlines opening weekend
description: The 2026/27 Premier League season is finally here, with the opening weekend set to offer the first taste of another thrilling campaign.From Arsenal’s bid to retain their crown to a host of new manag...
fullText:
The 2026/27 Premier League season is finally here, with the opening weekend set to offer the first taste of another thrilling campaign.

From Arsenal's bid to retain their crown to a host of new managers and promoted sides looking to make their mark, Matchday 1 promises to provide an early glimpse of what could lie ahead.

Buoyed by a 3-0 rout of Manchester City in the FA Community Shield, Arsenal kick off their Premier League title defence against newly promoted Coventry City at the Emirates Stadium.

Frank Lampard's men head into proceedings as massive underdogs, looking to end the Gunners' all-time competition record of 45 consecutive unbeaten home games against newcomers.

This will be the first top-flight meeting between the sides since 2001, but Coventry's dismal run of just one win from their last 14 such clashes against Arsenal speaks volumes.

Hull City's promotion was nothing short of miraculous, yet their first Premier League campaign since 2016/17 starts against a side they have not beaten in the league since 1974.

Manchester United's formidable record against the Tigers offers them plenty of encouragement as they bid to build on a strong finish to the 2025/26 season under Michael Carrick.

With no side boasting more victories on the opening matchday in Premier League history than the Red Devils' 22, the stage looks set for the visitors' statement win right from the outset.

Everton's second season at the Hill Dickinson Stadium commences with a favourable clash against Crystal Palace, whose new manager Pierre Sage hopes to impress on his Premier League debut.

Sage, who replaced Oliver Glasner at the end of last season, will also look to become only the third Eagles boss ever to win their first Premier League game in charge of the club.

David Moyes could go eight straight league games without a win for the first time as Everton manager, but with Palace winning just once in their last 23 top-flight matches against them, that may not happen.

Portman Road sets the stage for the first Premier League showdown between Ipswich Town and Sunderland since 2001, with the visitors seeking a third consecutive opening-day triumph.

Gary O'Neil will be keen to stop the Black Cats in their tracks on his Premier League return, as he replaced Kieran McKenna in the summer after a decent Ligue 1 stint with Strasbourg.

However, Sunderland finished last season on a high, winning their final two league outings, which puts them in a position to claim three successive top-flight wins for the first time since 2014.

After winning the Europa Conference League with Palace last term, Glasner has been entrusted with leading Nottingham Forest into life without Elliot Anderson, but the City Ground may not be an ideal place to start his new adventure.

Forest emerged victorious from just one of their last nine home league fixtures, yet Leeds United's visit could help change that narrative. The Tricky Trees have won both Premier League home clashes against this opposition in the 21st century.

The Whites' unenviable return of just two away league victories last season makes the hosts a far more appealing option to start the season with three points.

The first of the two opening-day London derbies takes place at the Gtech Community Stadium, where Brentford take on a new-look Tottenham Hotspur in an unfavourable match-up for the home team.

Despite finishing well above Spurs in the last two seasons, the Bees have won just one of their ten historical Premier League matches against them and are still waiting for their first home victory over them in the top flight.

Keen to avoid another embarrassing campaign, Spurs have spent big this summer to sign Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke, showing a clear statement of intent.

Brighton & Hove Albion's five-game unbeaten opening-day run in the Premier League perhaps best illustrates the magnitude of the task awaiting Aston Villa at the Amex Stadium this weekend.

Unai Emery inspired Villa to Europa League glory last term, but it's anyone's guess how they will fare after losing Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer,

Villa have lost just two of their 14 previous Premier League meetings with the Seagulls, which should boost their confidence ahead of the game.

Enzo Maresca blamed Riccardo Calafiori's early opener for Man City's chastening Community Shield defeat, and he'll look to atone on his competitive debut at the Etihad Stadium.

Bournemouth could not have imagined a worse place to begin life without Andoni Iraola than the Etihad, where they've lost all nine Premier League visits, conceding three or more goals in eight of those losses.

It'll be up to new boss Marco Rose to buck that ominous trend, but the odds are heavily stacked against the Cherries for a reason.

Liverpool travel to St James' Park to face Newcastle United without Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate, who have left this summer.

It's a new dawn following an underwhelming title-defending campaign last term, and Virgil van Dijk has confirmed that 'everyone is up for the challenge' during the pre-match conference.

Liverpool's strong run of 19 consecutive unbeaten league matches against Newcastle does little to inspire confidence for the home side. Neither do the high-profile summer sales of Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes and Tonali.

Matchday one ends at Craven Cottage, where former Real Madrid manager Alvaro Arbeloa begins his new chapter in English football against a Chelsea side hoping to turn the page under Xabi Alonso.

Fulham appointed the Spaniard in the wake of Marco Silva's move to Benfica in a desperate attempt to improve on last season's 11th-place finish and bounce back from an erratic end to the campaign.

Chelsea finished last season narrowly ahead of the Cottagers, highlighting just how much work awaits Alonso if he is to meet the lofty expectations at Stamford Bridge.

title: Real Madrid summer signing names Cristiano Ronaldo his idol: ‘The pictures say everything’
description: Real Madrid signed talented Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig this summer for a mammoth fee of €140 million.That price tag was a clear reflection of the kind of faith Los Blancos had i...
fullText:
Real Madrid signed talented Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig this summer for a mammoth fee of €140 million.

That price tag was a clear reflection of the kind of faith Los Blancos had in the teenage sensation who had taken the Bundesliga by storm last season.

After signing for Madrid, Diomande reiterated that he was honoured to play for the Spanish club and that he was not feeling the pressure of the price tag.

Now, speaking to Sporty TV in an interview, the African winger has admitted that he idolised Cristiano Ronaldo growing up.

"Cristiano Ronaldo is my idol," Diomande said.

The winger is now walking through the same training facilities where Ronaldo spent some of the greatest years of his career, and the photographs around the club have clearly made an impression on Madrid's new signing.

"When I go to training, I look at his pictures. The pictures say everything," he explained.

"The walk, the aura. I'm proud to play in the club my idol played in."

For a young attacker arriving at Madrid with enormous expectations, there could hardly be a more appropriate reference point.

Ronaldo's legacy at Real Madrid needs little introduction.

His combination of goals, personality, relentless ambition and ability to perform under pressure transformed him into one of the defining players in the club's history.

Diomande is obviously at the very beginning of his own Madrid journey, and comparisons between the two would be premature.

However, if Diomande could even imbibe some of the mentality that Ronaldo showed, it would set him up for success in a massive way.

Yan Diomande is Real Madrid's record signing. (Photo courtesy: Real Madrid official website)

The Ivorian has made no attempt to hide what joining Madrid means to him.

He previously described the club's call as a dream, admitting he could barely sleep after learning of their interest.

Now he is training surrounded by reminders of the player who helped shape that dream in the first place.

There will inevitably be pressure and difficult moments ahead. Diomande is young, the expectations are enormous and Jose Mourinho has serious competition throughout his attack.

However, if there is something Diomande can learn from his idol, it is that failures are always stepping stones to success.

Ronaldo never gave up in spite of the numerous times that he was written off and, perhaps, Madrid fans are getting ready to see Diomande write the next iconic chapter at the Santiago Bernabeu.
